content.title: About
content.content: Dosa is a thin, crispy crepe made from a fermented batter of rice and black gram (urad dal), a staple of South Indian cuisine. Plain dosa is served without filling and is usually accompanied by chutney, sambar, or a drizzle of oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The batter ferments for 8–12 hours, giving the dosa its characteristic mild sour taste.
Dosa has a low glycemic index thanks to the fermentation process.
In South India dosa is commonly eaten for breakfast but is enjoyed at any time of day.
There are more than 30 regional variations, including masala dosa with a spiced potato filling.
The batter’s thin consistency allows a dosa to cook in 1–2 minutes on a hot skillet.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that support gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Traditional plain dosa is cooked with little to no oil, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Black gram provides a good amount of amino acids.

items.title: Source of iron and B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice and black gram supply iron, thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for energy and blood formation.

items.title: Blood‑sugar regulation
items.content: The low glycemic index helps maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to black gram.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Traditional dosa is gluten‑free, but some commercial mixes may contain gluten additives.

items.title: Bacterial spoilage if improperly fermented
items.content: Leaving the batter at too high a temperature can cause it to spoil.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot dosa rolled or folded, with coconut chutney, sambar, yogurt, or a drizzle of melted butter. It can also be used as a wrap for vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly cooked dosa is best eaten immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Frozen dosa can be reheated on a dry skillet.
